entries.shortExplanation: 티머니 means "T-money (transit card)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 티머니 (timeoni) means "T-money (transit card)". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 티머니 주세요 ("A T-money card, please."). In Korean the particle or ending next to 티머니 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about using buses, subways, taxis, and asking where to get on or off, then change a single part.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 티머니 주세요. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 티머니.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about using buses, subways, taxis, and asking where to get on or off. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

examples.en: I bought a T-money card at the convenience store.

entries.nuance: 티머니 (T-money) is the most common rechargeable transit card. You buy and recharge it at convenience stores and stations, and use it on subways, buses, and many taxis.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Do not say 티머니를 충전돼요; say 티머니를 충전해요 or 충전해 주세요.

entries.explanation: "charge / top-up" is 충전 (chungjeon). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 충전해 주세요 ("Please charge it / top it up."). Watch the particle attached to 충전 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. 충전 adds balance; do not confuse it with 결제, which means making a payment.

entries.shortExplanation: 택배 means "parcel delivery" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "parcel delivery" is 택배 (taekbae). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 택배가 왔어요 ("A package arrived."). Watch the particle attached to 택배 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options first, then vary one word.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 택배가 왔어요. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 택배.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about buying things, checking prices, quantities, and payment options. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.en: Please leave it at the door.

examples.en: The package has not arrived yet.

entries.nuance: 택배 is courier parcel delivery (for example CJ대한통운 or 우체국). You track it with a 송장 번호 (tracking number); convenience-store drop-off and pickup are common.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
택배 is parcel courier service; 배달 usually means food delivery, which is a different service.

entries.shortExplanation: 미세먼지 means "fine dust (air pollution)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 미세먼지 (misemeonji) = "fine dust (air pollution)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 미세먼지가 많아요 ("There is a lot of fine dust.") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 미세먼지, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs and swap just one element to make it yours.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 미세먼지가 많아요. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 미세먼지.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.en: There is a lot of fine dust.
How is the fine dust today?

examples.en: The fine dust is bad today.
I wear a mask because of the fine dust.
The fine dust level is bad.

entries.nuance: 미세먼지 is fine dust or air pollution, reported daily as 좋음(good), 보통(normal), 나쁨(bad), and 매우 나쁨(very bad). On bad days people wear masks and limit outdoor time.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
미세먼지 (PM10) and 초미세먼지 (PM2.5) are reported separately; check both.
